newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex open seen firmer ahead of API's.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex open seen firmer ahead of API's.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were called to open little changed to five cents firmer on Wednesday, while crude products were expected to open 0.25 to 0.40 cent higher.
IPE Brent crude was barely firmer, rising one cent to $19.23 a barrel as of 0855 EDT/1255 GMT.

Traders said the modestly firmer tone in London, the severity of Tuesday's tumble on NYMEX and the uncertainty leading up to Wednesday's American Petroleum Institute inventory report should keeping trading humble.
July crude futures on NYMEX fell 84 cents Tuesday, settling at $20.79 a barrel.
"If this market is going to have a chance, we have to get back above $21.00 and stay there," one floor broker said.
Early talk among traders called for today's API figures to show flat to slightly higher inventory levels, with refinery usage rates remaining at or slightly below current levels.
In Singapore, Exxon declined to comment on sourced reports that Esso Singapore had cut output at its 230,000 bpd refinery by about 10 percent.
